Why Firsty is different in Thailand

Same price as everywhere else Thailand's cheap. Your data should be too. €0.98 per GB on Prepaid, from €2/day on Unlimited, the same as in Vietnam, Japan or Italy. No Southeast Asia surcharge, no island premium.
Buy data that never expires Most travel eSIMs make you buy GBs that expire in 7 or 30 days: use it or lose it. With Firsty Prepaid, the GBs you buy stay on your account forever. Bought 10 GB and only used 4 between Bangkok and Krabi? The other 6 are still there for Bali, Hanoi, or anywhere else.

Countries, 1 eSIM
One eSIM, every country Doing Thailand as part of a bigger Southeast Asia loop? Your Firsty eSIM also works in Vietnam, Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, and 176 other countries: same eSIM, same app, no reinstall.

How it works

How Firsty works in Thailand

Network coverage
Strongest local network
Firsty automatically connects to a strong local network, AIS or True, so you get signal on the BTS Skytrain and MRT in Bangkok, in Chiang Mai's Old City, on Phuket's beaches and around Ao Nang in Krabi. No manual switching, no APN setup.
Quick activation
Activation in 60 seconds
Download the Firsty app, sign up, tap "Activate." Your eSIM installs automatically: no QR code, no email to wait for. Set it up before you leave, and it activates the moment you land at Suvarnabhumi, Don Mueang, or Phuket.
No more worries
Stop worrying about data
Bought too much? It rolls over. Bought too little? Top up instantly in the app. Bought a day pass? Pause it on your lazy beach day in Koh Lanta.

Bangkok + the islands

~10 - 15 GB Post videos while you wait for the ferry, hotspot for your laptop, or video call home. Prepaid 10 GB for €17, or Unlimited 7-day pass, €19.25 total.
10+ days

Backpacker / remote worker

Unlimited Zoom calls from a Chiang Mai café, streaming in your hostel bunk, hotspot all day. Firsty Unlimited drops to €2.20/day once you hit 20 days, or the Monthly subscription at €59 if you're staying a while.

Where in Thailand does Firsty work?

Bangkok: Fast 4G and 5G in Sukhumvit, Silom and Siam, and along the BTS and MRT lines. Chiang Mai & the north: Reliable in the Old City and Nimman. Short dead zones on the winding road to Pai. Phuket: Strong 4G with 5G in the main towns and beach areas. Koh Samui: Strong on Chaweng and Lamai beaches; weaker in the hilly interior. Krabi, Koh Phi Phi & Koh Lanta: Good around Ao Nang and Lanta's west coast; patchy in remote bays and no signal mid-ferry. Pattaya: 4G and 5G across the city.

Questions? We've got you.

We know, it sounds too good to be true. But it’s real. Here’s how.

What are the eSIM plans available in Thailand?

The best eSIM plans available in Thailand cater to various data needs. Firsty offers both free and paid plans for seamless connectivity. With Firsty Free, you get ad-supported data for basic internet use. For heavy data users needing high-speed internet for streaming and video calls, First Class is perfect, especially in vibrant cities like Bangkok, Chiang Mai, and Phuket.

How can I activate a travel eSIM for Thailand?

Activating a travel eSIM for Thailand is a breeze:

  1. Ensure you have a stable Wi-Fi connection to download the Firsty app.

  2. Open the app and follow the super easy setup process to activate your free eSIM.

  3. When you arrive in Thailand, your connection will be ready instantly.

  4. For faster internet, upgrade to Comfort+ or First Class, which you can purchase and activate anytime without needing WiFi.

Is it worth getting an eSIM for Thailand?

Yes, if you want to skip the airport queue and keep your home SIM in your phone. Thai tourist SIMs are cheap, but you'll need your passport, a face scan and a SIM swap. Firsty installs before you fly and connects the moment you land.

What's the best eSIM for Thailand?

The one that fits your trip. For a few days of maps and messaging, Firsty Free costs nothing. For island-hopping with hotspot, Unlimited from €2/day means no counting. Doing Thailand plus Vietnam or Japan? One Firsty eSIM covers them all at the same price.

Does Firsty work everywhere in Thailand?

In cities, resorts and on the main islands, yes. Firsty uses Thailand's major networks, AIS and True, which cover Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Phuket, Krabi and Koh Samui well. Expect gaps on ferry crossings, in remote bays and on mountain roads up north.

Can I use my Firsty eSIM as a hotspot in Thailand?

Yes. Share your data with your laptop or a travel buddy on Prepaid or Unlimited. On Unlimited you get 5 GB a day at high speed, then 512 Kbps until your next day or top-up, so save big downloads for hotel Wi-Fi.

Can I make calls and send SMS with Firsty in Thailand?

Firsty is a data eSIM: calls and texts work through LINE, WhatsApp, FaceTime, or any internet-based app. International calling to 200+ countries is available through the Firsty app at transparent per-minute rates.

Where in Thailand does Firsty work?
Bangkok: Fast 4G and 5G in Sukhumvit, Silom and Siam, and along the BTS and MRT lines. Chiang Mai & the north: Reliable in the Old City and Nimman. Short dead zones on the winding road to Pai. Phuket: Strong 4G with 5G in the main towns and beach areas. Koh Samui: Strong on Chaweng and Lamai beaches; weaker in the hilly interior. Krabi, Koh Phi Phi & Koh Lanta: Good around Ao Nang and Lanta's west coast; patchy in remote bays and no signal mid-ferry. Pattaya: 4G and 5G across the city.

Does Firsty work everywhere in Thailand?
In cities, resorts and on the main islands, yes. Firsty uses Thailand's major networks, AIS and True, which cover Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Phuket, Krabi and Koh Samui well. Expect gaps on ferry crossings, in remote bays and on mountain roads up north.

Can I make calls and send SMS with Firsty in Thailand?
